features.title: Grain coherence
features.notes: How rank-one the structure tensor is, 0 to 1. On this terrain it sits above 0.98 for three quarters of the cells, so it does not separate cells with a grain from cells without one and must not be used as a quality filter. sources.title: EM conductors (interpreted)
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: Graphitic basement units are "the source of most significant conductors in the Athabasca Basin, and are key empirical locators for U deposits" (Jefferson et al. 2007, via research report 02 section 1.1.3). This is the single most valuable public feature here.
caveats: Conductor traces plot up-dip of blind ore, so a buffer must extend down-dip rather than being symmetric (report 02, 1.1.3).
Silicification can turn graphitic gneiss from a conductor into a resistor, so absence is not evidence of absence.
The Wolverine Point Formation is itself a conductor and hinders detection of graphitic units beneath it.
Attribute list not yet confirmed: do not assume a conductance field exists.
Compiled as it stands today, partly from surveys flown after the discoveries it now sits near: a hindcast using it is optimistic.

sources.title: Faults and lineaments, 1:250,000
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: The trap element: "the unconformity offset where footwall faults meet the P2 fault hosts the McArthur River ore pods" (report 02, 1.1.5). Fault intersections matter more than fault proximity alone.
caveats: YEAR was 0 in every sampled row: treat it as unpopulated, not as a compilation date.
A 1:250,000 line has map-scale position error far larger than an ore body.

sources.title: Bedrock geology, 1:250,000
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: Magnetic lows mark "pelitic-psammopelitic gneiss, the host of graphitic conductors" (report 02, 1.1.2); with no public magnetic grid, the mapped lithology is the only way to reach that element. LITHOLOGY carries the graphitic and pelitic descriptors a criterion can key on.
caveats: Better than the 1:1,000,000 compilation already pulled, but still a regional map.

sources.title: Surficial geology, 1:250,000
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: Whether a surface sample means anything depends on what lies between it and bedrock; also the glacial context for boulder dispersal.
caveats: Two attributes only: it classifies the environment, not the thickness of cover.

sources.title: Lake sediment geochemistry (Geological Survey of Canada analyses)
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: The densest direct uranium pathfinder available publicly; U_INA is neutron activation.
caveats: Uranium in lake sediment is a dispersion signal, not a deposit: it says something upstream is shedding uranium.
Sampling is lake-limited, so a cell with no lake has no measurement rather than a low one.

sources.title: Lake sediment geochemistry (provincial survey, 1975-1978)
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: Collected 1975-1978 around the Athabasca sandstone, before most mining: a pre-mining baseline (report 02, 1.2).
caveats: Same lake-limited sampling frame; carries its own year field, so it can be used in a dated hindcast.

sources.title: Lake water geochemistry
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: Small but carries pH and Eh, which let a uranium-in-water anomaly be conditioned rather than read raw.
caveats: 566 points over a narrow latitude band: coverage is thin and the readiness scorecard must say so.

sources.title: Radioactive boulders
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: A boulder train is a vector, not a location: at Patterson Lake the discovery hole cut over 1% U3O8 3.8 km up-ice of the boulders (report 02, 1.2). The only layer here with a populated year, so it also dates exploration effort.
caveats: The source lies up-ice, so the criterion is a corridor in the ice-flow direction, not a buffer.
Zircon in till travelled over 100 km up-ice in one study: transport distance is not fixed.

sources.title: Magnetic domains (interpreted)
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: Interpreted domain polygons: the nearest public stand-in for a magnetic grid, which is not published by URL.
caveats: An interpretation, not a measurement.
Report 02 records that the magnetic signature is contested: most deposits sit on magnetic lows, yet others 'lack characteristic magnetic signatures'. A criterion must not assume a fixed sign.

sources.title: Minerals and Quaternary Drillhole Compilation
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: Two jobs: the depth fields interpolate an unconformity-depth surface, and DATE_DRILLED gives the effort model its dated drilling history. Holds no assay or lithology values.
caveats: Depth fields are populated only where a hole reached the contact, so the interpolation carries its own coverage count.

sources.title: Canadian Aeromagnetic Data Base: 200 m residual total magnetic field grid (national compilation)
sources.licence: Open Government Licence - Canada
sources.notes: Published, open-licensed, not yet pulled: the resource link redirects to geophysical-data.canada.ca and the portal's download route is still to be driven. Magnetic lows over graphitic basement are the classic Athabasca pathway proxy; when pulled this replaces the interpreted magnetic-domains stand-in. Last data 2018, grid updated 2020.
caveats: A national compilation of surveys flown at 800 m line spacing before 2000: coarser than the company surveys in the assessment files, and it is a residual field, not an interpretation.

sources.title: Assessment survey footprints (airborne, ground, underground)
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: Where surveys were flown or walked: a direct measure of exploration effort, and the backbone of the null model. Layers 0 and 1 carry the underground and ground surveys.
caveats: A footprint says a survey happened, not what it measured: this is effort, never a geophysical value.

sources.title: Athabasca Supergroup outline (1:1,000,000 bedrock geology)
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: Defines the study area. Buffered 30 km so the margin discoveries at Patterson Lake fall inside the grid.

sources.title: GeoDS subsurface drilling layer
sources.licence: no licence stated
sources.notes: A second drilling history, keyed to assessment files. Used but never redistributed.
caveats: No licence stated, so the public-safe build keeps only what is matched to redistributable records.

sources.title: Uranium deposit footprints
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: The positive class, tier A. Named, but carrying no deposit type, grade, tonnage or date.
caveats: A label, never a feature: using it as an input is leakage, and a test enforces that.
SOURCE holds report titles with publication dates, which are a lagging and biased proxy for discovery, not a discovery date.

sources.title: Saskatchewan Mineral Deposit Index, uranium-primary records
sources.licence: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence v2.0
sources.notes: 6,012 records in all, 1,698 uranium-primary, 1,989 inside the region box. The weaker positive tier: an occurrence is a place uranium was observed, not a deposit.
caveats: DISCOVERYTYPE is a method (Drillhole, Lake Sediment, Outcrop grab), not a year: there is no discovery date in this layer.
PRODUCTION and RESERVESRESOURCES are yes/no flags with no grade or tonnage.
Occurrences sit where people looked, which is what the null model exists to measure.

sources.title: Sentinel-2 L2A surface reflectance
sources.licence: Copernicus Sentinel Data Licence
sources.notes: COGs on the public sentinel-cogs bucket; a SWIR asset returned HTTP 200 unauthenticated and a 0.5 by 0.3 degree box over the basin matched 27 scenes under 10% cloud in one summer. Jobs: a lake and wetland mask (the sampling frame for the lake geochemistry), cover versus outcrop, and true-colour and SWIR chips for each candidate cell.
caveats: Athabasca deposits sit 100 to 900 m down under 1 to 2 km of sandstone: no optical sensor sees them, and this layer is never an ore detector here.
A frontier model scored 0.369 on geological map understanding (report 02, 4.4), so an agent may describe ground context from a chip but must not claim alteration from it.
Clay alteration is detectable by SWIR only where it reaches the surface; in this basin it generally does not.

sources.title: Copernicus DEM GLO-30
sources.licence: Copernicus Sentinel Data Licence
sources.notes: Terrain, drainage, and the orientation of glacial landforms, which is what turns a radioactive boulder field into an up-ice search corridor.
caveats: The STAC asset href is an s3:// URL; read it through the public HTTPS mirror.
Ice-flow direction inferred from landform orientation is an interpretation, and the criterion carries it as one.

sources.title: Landsat Collection 2 Level 2
sources.licence: USGS public domain
sources.notes: Archive to 1982, so it can show ground as it looked before a discovery: useful context for the hindcast.
caveats: 30 m and older sensors; used for change and context, not for measurement.

sources.title: Sentinel-1 GRD radar
sources.licence: Copernicus Sentinel Data Licence
sources.notes: Deferred. Eight scenes matched over the basin, but the assets are SAFE manifests and calibration schemas, not analysis-ready COGs, so using it means building a preprocessing chain this demo does not need yet.

sources.title: Assay intervals read from assessment reports
sources.licence: no licence stated
sources.notes: The province publishes no assay values, so every uranium grade in this system came out of a PDF. That makes these intervals the one label source no public layer can supply, and an optional second positive class.
caveats: Tier B: read by a model and unvalidated until a check says otherwise. Every value carries its page, box, quote and validator outcomes.
A class-A flagged value may not silently become a label: the model is run with and without this source, and both results are reported.
Four files read so far, so the coverage is tiny and clustered; it cannot be treated as a survey of the basin.

gaps.title: Airborne magnetic, radiometric and gravity grids
gaps.why_it_matters: Magnetics and radiometrics are the standard first-pass Athabasca datasets, and gravity carries the quartz-dissolution signal. Their absence is the biggest hole in any public model of this basin.
gaps.evidence: Re-verified 2026-09-19 (PRD section B, Phase 2): the earlier 'not addressable' was wrong on magnetics. Natural Resources Canada publishes the Canadian Aeromagnetic Data Base compilation on the Open Government Portal under the Open Government Licence - Canada (dataset 752fe3fc-d871-5ae1-9bd9-2b6f65880a8d, modified 2020-10-05) with resources 'Canada - 200m - MAG - Residual Total Field' (ZIP), 'Canada - 1km - MAG - Residual Total Field', both first vertical derivatives, and a CAGDB WMS (images, not values). The file links (gdr.agg.nrcan.gc.ca dapid=140) redirect to the new portal at geophysical-data.canada.ca, whose download path has not yet been driven; the Northern Saskatchewan 100 m compilation lives behind the same portal. Radiometrics and gravity: unchanged, no value grid found. The provincial Geophysics service still publishes survey footprints only.
gaps.workaround: Until the 200 m grid is pulled: mapped lithology and interpreted magnetic domains stand in for the magnetic-low proxy; nothing stands in for radiometrics or gravity. The pull is a Phase 2 task, not a research question.

gaps.title: Discovery dates for deposits and occurrences
gaps.why_it_matters: Without them there is no honest train-before, test-after split, which is the strongest test available short of drilling.
gaps.evidence: No discovery-year, year-found or first-reported field exists in the SMDI REST layer or on an SMDI detail page; DISCOVERYTYPE is a method. Deposit footprints carry only report titles. Checked 2026-09-18.
gaps.workaround: A hand-built table of about ten dated discoveries, each cited to a public technical report, used only as a hold-out; plus leave-one-camp-out spatial folds, which need no dates.

gaps.title: Conductance or strength on the EM conductor layer
gaps.why_it_matters: The folklore that stronger conductors make better targets could only be tested with a conductance value.
gaps.evidence: Feature count confirmed at 28,458; the attribute list was not enumerated. Checked 2026-09-18.
gaps.workaround: Criteria use distance and density only. The strength claims stay in the handbook marked as untested folklore, with weight zero.

gaps.title: Clay alteration and geochemical footprints at depth
gaps.why_it_matters: Alteration is the largest expression of the system: the Cigar Lake halo reaches about 100 m below and 300 m above the unconformity.
gaps.evidence: Halo extents and Hinckley index ranges exist in the literature, but the measurements are in company drill logs, not in any public layer. Report 02 section 1.2.
gaps.workaround: None. The handbook states the extents so an agent can say what would settle a cell, and the adjudicator is required to name it as an unknown rather than an absence.
